slo_title: Apply these identities to evaluate definite integrals

mcq.q: \(\text{Parseval's identity for Fourier cosine transforms applied to two functions } f(x) \text{ and } g(x) \text{ states:}\)

\(\text{Given } F_c\{e^{-x}\} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{1}{1+s^2} \text{ and } F_c\{e^{-2x}\} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{2}{4+s^2}, \text{ use Parseval's identity to find } \int_0^\infty \frac{dx}{(x^2+1)^2}.\)
\(\text{For } a=2, b=3, \text{ the value of } \int_0^\infty \frac{dx}{(x^2+4)(x^2+9)} \text{ using Parseval's identity is:}\)
\(\text{Using Parseval's identity for Fourier cosine transforms with } f(x)=e^{-ax} \text{ and } g(x)=e^{-bx}, \text{ evaluate } \int_0^\infty \frac{dx}{(x^2+a^2)(x^2+b^2)}.\)
\(\text{Using Parseval's identity for Fourier sine transforms with } f(x)=e^{-ax} \text{ and } g(x)=e^{-bx}, \text{ what integral would be evaluated?}\)

sq.q: \(\text{State Parseval's identity for Fourier sine transform and use it to evaluate } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{x^2}{(x^2+1)^2} dx.\)
\(\text{State Parseval's identity for Fourier cosine transform and use it to evaluate } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{dx}{(x^2+1)^2}.\)

lq.q: \(\text{State Parseval's identities for Fourier cosine and sine transforms.}\)
answer: Step Marks For Fourier cosine transform: \(\int_{0}^{\infty} [f(x)]^2 dx = \int_{0}^{\infty} [F_c(s)]^2 ds\) (3) For Fourier sine transform: \(\int_{0}^{\infty} [f(x)]^2 dx = \int_{0}^{\infty} [F_s(s)]^2 ds\) (3) where \(F_c(s) = \mathcal{F}_c\{f(x)\}\) and \(F_s(s) = \mathcal{F}_s\{f(x)\}\) (2) General form: \(\int_{0}^{\infty} f(x)g(x) dx = \int_{0}^{\infty} F_c(s)G_c(s) ds = \int_{0}^{\infty} F_s(s)G_s(s) ds\) (4)
